rationale: dispatch_context_menu resolved a target and fired only that view's on_context_menu, with no target-to-root walk. Every other pointer verb in pointer_dispatch.cpp already walks: capture_path_to_root builds the bubble path for pointerdown, pointermove, pointerup and click, and the click path additionally walks click_target to its parent. The context-menu verb was the one exception, and it is the one where the DOM's own semantics make bubbling load-bearing: contextmenu bubbles, so a page routinely puts the listener on a wrapper and paints a canvas or an absolutely-positioned overlay on top of it with no listener of its own. The hit test correctly returns that child, the child has no callback, and the press is dropped -- the wrapper's handler never runs even though the press landed inside it. Measured on exactly that tree in a bridge test: a child panel created over a subscribed wrapper takes the hit test, and before this change the dispatch returned false. The walk now starts at the target, stops at root, fires the first view that carries a callback, and returns false only when none does. The nearest handler wins and the walk stops there, which matches the single on_context_menu slot a View carries; this is a bubble to the first listener, not a fan-out to every ancestor, so no view that previously received a callback stops receiving one and no view receives one twice. The coordinates handed to that callback are still point_to_local against the view that actually handles it, not against the view that was hit, so a wrapper reads the press in its own space. No public signature moved: both dispatch_context_menu overloads keep their declarations in pointer_dispatch.hpp. No host branches on the return value -- window_host_mac.mm and plugin_view_host_mac.mm discard it and repaint, and win_plugin_input_router.hpp discards it -- so a press that now reports handled where it previously reported unhandled changes no platform fallback. Nothing about left-button routing, capture, focus, wheel, scroll, gesture arbitration or the down/drag/up contracts changed. This is Pulp-only. The defect shape is an artifact of Pulp having grown each pointer verb separately against a retained tree, so a verb added later missed a walk the earlier ones had; a Vellum-native retained UI kernel should deliver every pointer-derived event through one propagation pipeline in which a verb cannot silently lack a phase, rather than as a set of independently written verbs. There is no named immutable Vellum framework commit being backported here, and this records no Vellum acknowledgement.
